question: Should I wear a mask outside in Singapore today?
name: Claude
answer:
**Yes, probably. Singapore is having a haze episode, so a mask is a good idea if you'll be outdoors for a while.** The latest reports I found are from 17 October 2026, so check the live readings before you go out.

**Conditions on 17 Oct**
- At 2pm the 24-hour PSI was "unhealthy" in every region: central (184), north (135), south (154), east (173) and west (185).
- Central Singapore had been "very unhealthy" the day before, peaking at 229.
- By 7pm, hourly PM2.5 was in the "high" band in the south (156µg/m3), central (182) and west (198).
- The east and north were "elevated".
- The smoke is drifting in from fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra. NEA expects showers and a change in wind direction to ease it, but some haze may keep coming from Sumatra.

**What I'd do**
- **Short, quick trips** (for example, walking to the MRT): a mask is optional for healthy adults.
- **Long periods outdoors, or strenuous exercise:** wear a mask, or move the activity indoors.
- **Children, older people, pregnant women, and people with asthma, heart or lung conditions:** wear a mask and limit time outside.
- **Which mask:** a surgical or cloth mask won't filter fine particles well. An N95 is the right choice, and it needs to fit snugly.
- **Free N95s:** the government has started handing out N95 masks to vulnerable Singaporeans through Community Clubs and vending machines at selected hubs. You can check eligibility and stock on the HazeMaskGoWhere website (go.gov.sg/hazemask).

**Live readings**
- Use the NEA haze site or the myENV app for the 1-hour PM2.5 reading in your area. NEA says to use it for immediate outdoor activities.
- Check it before going out, because the readings can change quickly with rain and wind.

If you're in the north or east and the reading is lower, you can be more relaxed. If you're in the central, west or south, I'd wear one.

# Singapore haze keeps air quality unhealthy across island, with PM2.5 levels high in most regions
Pasir Panjang Terminal shrouded in haze as seen from Labrador Park at 10.15 am on Oct 17.

SINGAPORE; Hazy conditions persisted into the afternoon of Oct 17, even as the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in central Singapore dipped back into the “unhealthy” band after remaining in the “very unhealthy” range the previous day.

At 2pm, the 24-hour PSI was in the “unhealthy” range in all regions: central (184), north (135), south (154), east (173) and west (185).

Meanwhile, hourly PM2.5 readings entered the “high” range in the west at 158 at 11am, followed by the central and southern regions at noon and the east at 2pm.



At 2pm, hourly PM2.5 readings stood at 243 in the west, 179 in the central region, 162 in the south and 159 in the east. The figure remained in the “elevated” range in the north at 91.

Air quality is considered “unhealthy” when the PSI – a 24-hour rolling average of six key air pollutants – is between 101 and 200, and “very unhealthy” when it is between 201 and 300.

Hourly PM2.5 readings are measured in micrograms per cubic metre and used as an indicator of current air quality.

PM2.5 scores from 0 to 55 represent normal values, while readings between 56 and 150 indicate an elevated concentration of fine particles. Readings between 151 and 250 are considered high, while scores above 251 are classified as very high.

The central region was worst hit on Oct 16, when the 24-hour PSI remained in the “very unhealthy” range throughout the day, peaking at a seasonal high of 229 between 3pm and 4pm and remaining at that level until the early hours of Oct 17.
